chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no goodness in the child of adultery, nor in his skin, nor in his hair, nor in his flesh, nor in his blood, nor in anything from him. He was left out from the ship (of Noah), and the dog and the pig were carried therein.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of the child of adultery in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) declares that there is no goodness in the child of adultery, extending this lack of goodness to all physical parts of his body and everything belonging to him. This is illustrated by the example of Noah's Ark, where the illegitimate child was excluded while the dog and pig were included. This narration highlights the concept of 'lack of goodness' (la khayr) as a comprehensive spiritual and physical state, often interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating a distinct lineage or inherent characteristic rather than mere exclusion from salvation.
